WHY THIS MATTERS

every pin has a reason.

This exercise checks the wiring you've declared in the interface. It does not identify which holes your physical jumpers occupy. That's why Circuit Forensics also tracks visual evidence and unresolved connections.

ESP32 I²C pins can be configured in firmware.

01 / Connect your ESP32

Upload the supplied Arduino firmware first, then connect the board over USB. Chrome or Edge on localhost supports Web Serial. You approve the port connection.

No device connected. Waiting for real serial data…

02 / Choose a test

These are diagnostic commands, not guarantees that a module is present. GNSS detection needs correct TX/RX and UART configuration; buttons and buzzers require guided user checks.

I²C response ≠ proof of individual wires. A scan cannot identify every device. NEVER perform continuity tests on a powered circuit.

Your saved project will determine the available tests.
ASK THE BENCH / 006

ask a
better question.

A practical hardware partner, grounded in your components and saved wiring. Not a generic chatbot.

What's on your mind?

Try: “Why do I need a MAX30102?”, “Check my SDA/SCL wiring”, or “Which diagnostic should I run for GNSS?”

Your answer will appear here. Electrical facts come from the component profiles; the assistant cannot see hidden physical wires.

Current project context

A useful assistant knows its limits.

It uses declared pin connections and saved components, not invented electrical measurements. With Ollama, language generation runs on your own machine. If Ollama is unavailable, deterministic guidance remains usable.
